record.original_question: Is the list packing number of every planar graph at most 7? That is, does chi*_l(G) <= 7 hold for every planar graph G?

evidence.quote: The list packing number chi*_l(G) of G is the least k such that G admits an L-packing of size k for any k-list-assignment L of G.
Problem 2.7 Is it true that chi*_l(G) <= 7 for every planar graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph. A list assignment for G is a function L that assigns to each vertex v ∈ V a set L(v) of admissible colors. Given a positive integer k, L is called a k-list-assignment if |L(v)| = k for every v ∈ V. An L-coloring of G is a proper coloring c such that c(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V (i.e., c(u) ≠ c(v) whenever uv ∈ E and c(v) ∈ L(v) for all v).

An L-packing of size k of G is a collection (c_1, c_2, …, c_k) of k proper L-colorings of G that are pairwise permutation-disjoint at every vertex; more precisely, for every vertex v ∈ V, the multiset {c_1(v), c_2(v), …, c_k(v)} equals L(v) (so each color in L(v) is used exactly once at v across the k colorings).

The list packing number χ*_ℓ(G) of G is the least integer k such that for every k-list-assignment L of G, G admits an L-packing of size k.

Question: Does every planar graph G satisfy χ*_ℓ(G) ≤ 7?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2024 Cycles and Colourings workshop open problem collection. List packing is a recent notion (introduced around 2021), and while bounds for bounded-degree graphs have been studied, no published proof or refutation establishing χ*_ℓ(G) ≤ 7 for all planar graphs was found. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: List packing number of bounded degree graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies list packing numbers for bounded-degree graphs; no resolution for planar graphs with bound 7.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work treats list packing for restricted graph classes but does not resolve the planar bound 7.

status_evidence.title: A short proof that the list packing number of any graph is well defined
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that the list packing number is well-defined for every graph.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational results on list packing exist, but the planar-7 question is not addressed.
